author: s. j. bowles
title: Sunnyview Nursing and Rehabilitation Center had most beds among Butler County nursing homes in Q1
text:
Sunnyview Nursing and Rehabilitation Center was the biggest nursing home in Butler County during the opening quarter of 2026, data from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) shows .
The facility had a capacity of 220 beds—104 more than the Butler County average—during the first quarter of 2026, serving a typical census of 214 residents that period.
CMS assigned Sunnyview an overall cumulative score of 1 out of 5, lower than Pennsylvania’s average of 3 for nursing homes in the state.
For that period, Cranberry Place|St. John Specialty Care Center was the second largest in Butler County, offering 150 available beds.
By the end of Q1 2026, Sunnyview Nursing and Rehabilitation Center had incurred a single fine totaling $30,011 and received one penalty.
Altogether, six for-profit nursing homes operated in Butler County, Pennsylvania.
According to U.S. Census Bureau estimates , the senior population nationwide continues climbing while the younger demographic sees a decline. Americans age 65 and older rose by 13% between 2020 and 2024, while the population under 18 shrank by 1.7%. Over the past 100 years, the country’s older adult segment has soared from 4.9 million in 1920 to more than 61 million in 2024.
A 2021 analysis found that close to half—approximately 28 million—of that age group may require long-term services or support. The projection also suggested more than a third will likely need nursing home care at some point.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, an insurance education group. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
